sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Detailed study guide and resources for Vijayanagar Dynasties: Sangama are currently being prepared. Check back soon for comprehensive explanations, summary diagrams, and expert preparation recommendations.

Key Dimensions of Study:

  • Definition, scope, and foundational theories.
  • Relevance to General Studies Paper & Contemporary contexts.
  • Core applications and structural framework.

practiceQuestions.q: Who among the following brothers founded the Vijayanagar Empire in 1336 AD, laying the foundation of the Sangama dynasty?
opts: Deva Raya I and Deva Raya II
Tuluva Narasa Nayaka and Vira Narasimha
practiceQuestions.sol: The Vijayanagar Empire was founded in 1336 AD by Harihara and Bukka, who belonged to the Sangama dynasty and were sons of Sangama. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 History]

practiceQuestions.q: Which eminent saint and philosopher played a pivotal role in inspiring Harihara and Bukka to found the Vijayanagar Empire?
practiceQuestions.sol: Sage Vidyaranya, along with his brother Sayana, inspired Harihara and Bukka and guided them in establishing the empire and the city of Vijayanagar. [Primary Reference: NCERT Medieval India History]

practiceQuestions.q: The famous Italian traveler Nicolo de' Conti visited the Vijayanagar court during the reign of which Sangama ruler?
practiceQuestions.sol: Nicolo de' Conti, the Venetian traveler, visited Vijayanagar around 1420-1421 AD during the reign of Deva Raya I. [Primary Reference: Standard Historical Sources / IGNOU Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: Which Persian ambassador visited the court of Deva Raya II in the 15th century and left a detailed account of the Vijayanagar Empire?
practiceQuestions.sol: Abdur Razzaq, the ambassador of Shah Rukh of Persia, visited Vijayanagar during the reign of Deva Raya II and famously noted that 'the eye has not seen nor ear heard of any place like it'. [Primary Reference: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part II]

practiceQuestions.q: Who among the following Sangama rulers assumed the title 'Pratapadeva Raya' or 'Gajabetegara' (hunter of elephants)?
practiceQuestions.sol: Deva Raya II was the greatest ruler of the Sangama dynasty and assumed titles like 'Gajabetegara' (the hunter of elephants) and 'Immadi Deva Raya'. [Primary Reference: Archaeological Survey of India / Standard History Textbooks]

practiceQuestions.q: The famous mathematician and Vedic commentator Sayana belonged to the court of which dynasty of Vijayanagar?
practiceQuestions.sol: Sayana, along with his brother Madhava Vidyaranya, flourished under the patronage of the early Sangama kings (such as Bukka I and Harihara II), where he wrote commentaries on the Vedas. [Primary Reference: NCERT Cultural History]

practiceQuestions.q: Which river formed the northern boundary of the Vijayanagar Empire and was the perennial bone of contention with the Bahmani Sultanate?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Tungabhadra-Krishna river basin, particularly the Raichur Doab located between the Krishna and Tungabhadra rivers, was the primary zone of conflict between Vijayanagar and the Bahmani Sultanate. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 12 History]

practiceQuestions.q: Who was the last ruler of the Sangama dynasty, who was overthrown in 1485 AD to establish the Saluva dynasty?
practiceQuestions.sol: Virupaksha Raya II was the last weak ruler of the Sangama dynasty. He was assassinated by his son, and taking advantage of the turmoil, Saluva Narasimha overthrew the dynasty in 1485 AD, establishing the Saluva dynasty. [Primary Reference: IGNOU History Course / Standard Textbooks]

practiceQuestions.q: Which Sangama ruler successfully annexed Madurai, bringing the Sultanate of Madurai to an end?
practiceQuestions.sol: Kumara Kampana, the son of Bukka I, led a successful campaign against the Madurai Sultanate, which was famously chronicled in the Sanskrit work 'Madura Vijayam' written by his wife Gangadevi. [Primary Reference: NCERT Medieval History]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the capital city of the Vijayanagar Empire during the Sangama dynasty?
practiceQuestions.sol: The capital of the Vijayanagar Empire from its inception under the Sangama dynasty was Vijayanagar on the banks of the Tungabhadra River, modern-day Hampi. [Primary Reference: ASI / UNESCO World Heritage Site Documentation]

practiceQuestions.q: How did the administrative structure of the Sangama dynasty manage provincial governance, and what was the term used for the provinces?
opts: Divided into Mandalas or provinces headed by royal princes or trusted nobles
Direct bureaucratic control managed from the capital by centralized ministers
Delegated entirely to independent village assemblies without state interference
Controlled through a network of Islamic military governors appointed by the Sultan
practiceQuestions.sol: The Vijayanagar empire under the Sangama rulers was divided into provinces known as Mandalas, which were further subdivided into Nadus, Sthalas, and Gramas. Provinces were typically governed by royal princes (Mandaladhipatis) or high nobles. [Primary Reference: NCERT History / Epigraphical Evidence]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the significance of the military reforms introduced by Deva Raya II during the Sangama rule?
opts: He completely abolished infantry and relied solely on cavalry and elephants.
He inducted Muslim archers and cavalrymen into the Vijayanagar army to counter the Bahmani tactics.
He outsourced total military defense to foreign Portuguese mercenaries.
He disbanded the standing army and relied exclusively on feudal levies.
practiceQuestions.sol: Recognizing the military superiority of the Bahmani cavalry and archers, Deva Raya II reorganized his army by enlisting Muslim soldiers and archers, training them in native warfare, which significantly enhanced his military capabilities. [Primary Reference: Nilakanta Sastri, 'A History of South India']

practiceQuestions.q: Which economic sector generated the highest revenue for the state during the Sangama dynasty?
opts: Maritime overseas trade with Southeast Asia
Land revenue from agriculture (usually fixed at one-sixth of the produce)
Tribute extracted exclusively from European merchant colonies
Income derived purely from gold and diamond mining monopolies
practiceQuestions.sol: Land revenue was the principal source of income for the Vijayanagar state, typically assessed at one-sixth of the agricultural produce, supplemented by taxes on professions, shops, and trade. [Primary Reference: Economic History of South India / NCERT]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the nature of religious policy pursued by the Sangama rulers?
opts: Religious intolerance favoring exclusively Saivism and persecuting Vaishnavism and Islam
Profound religious tolerance, patronage of multiple sects, and integration of diverse traditions
Rigid adherence to orthodox Vedic rituals while banning all temple constructions
Mandatory state conversion of all subjects to specialized Bhakti sects
practiceQuestions.sol: Sangama rulers were staunch patrons of Hinduism (building temples and honoring sages like Vidyaranya) but maintained broad religious tolerance, employing Muslims in the military and respecting other faiths. [Primary Reference: Epigraphical Reports / NCERT]

practiceQuestions.q: How did the foreign trade dynamics under the Sangama dynasty contribute to the empire's power?
opts: It focused on importing superior war-horses from Arabia and Persia through western ports like Goa.
It was restricted entirely to exporting food grains to China under imperial edicts.
It relied exclusively on internal barter, rejecting external currency or maritime trade.
It prohibited private merchants from engaging in trade, maintaining a strict state monopoly.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Vijayanagar rulers, particularly during the Sangama and subsequent periods, maintained control over western ports (like Bhatkal and Goa) to import vital war-horses from Arabia and Persia, which were crucial for military success against northern sultanates. [Primary Reference: Hermann Kulke & Dietmar Rothermund, 'A History of India']

practiceQuestions.q: What was the significance of irrigation and public works in the agricultural strategy of the Sangama rulers?
opts: They ignored irrigation, depending solely on seasonal monsoon rainfall for dry crops.
They actively constructed dams, canals, and tanks (reservoirs) across rivers like the Tungabhadra to expand wet agriculture.
They banned the construction of reservoirs to prevent soil erosion and malaria.
Irrigation works were managed exclusively by foreign merchant guilds without state funding.
practiceQuestions.sol: To overcome the semi-arid conditions of the Deccan plateau, Sangama rulers invested heavily in water management systems, constructing extensive canals from the Tungabhadra river and large artificial reservoirs to boost paddy cultivation. [Primary Reference: Archaeological Excavations at Hampi / ASI]

practiceQuestions.q: How did the conflict between the Sangama dynasty and the Bahmani Sultanate shape geopolitical developments in South India?
opts: It resulted in permanent peace treaties and the peaceful unification of the Deccan.
It created a permanent state of military rivalry over fertile river zones, leading to shifting frontiers and strategic alliances.
It led to the total elimination of regional languages in favor of Persian administration.
It caused Vijayanagar to abandon peninsular politics and shift its capital to North India.
practiceQuestions.sol: The prolonged struggle between Vijayanagar (Sangama rulers) and the Bahmani Sultanate revolved around control of the Raichur Doab, Krishna-Godavari delta, and Konkan ports, defining the balance of power in medieval peninsular India. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 12 History]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the role of literature and language patronage under the Sangama kings?
opts: They patronized only Sanskrit, strictly banning Telugu and Kannada literature.
They patronized multiple languages, including Sanskrit, Kannada, and Telugu, laying the groundwork for classical literary growth.
They exclusively supported Arabic and Persian literary works to foster foreign relations.
They discouraged all courtly literature, promoting only folk oral traditions.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Sangama rulers supported scholars in Sanskrit (like Sayana and Madhava), Kannada, and Telugu, reflecting a rich multilingual cultural environment that continued throughout Vijayanagar history. [Primary Reference: Cultural History of South India / NCERT]

practiceQuestions.q: How did the administrative framework of the Sangama era handle urban administration and trade guilds?
opts: Trade guilds enjoyed significant autonomy in internal management, and major cities had organized mercantile quarters.
Guilds were abolished by royal decree to establish absolute state control over retail markets.
Urban administration was entirely handed over to foreign ambassadors.
Mercantile activities were heavily taxed out of existence, leading to ruralization.
practiceQuestions.sol: Vijayanagar cities were vibrant commercial centers where powerful merchant guilds (such as the Ainuruvar/500 swamis) regulated trade, set market standards, and interacted closely with imperial officers. [Primary Reference: Epigraphical and Numismatic Evidence / ASI]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the strategic importance of the city of Vijayanagar's location on the Tungabhadra river?
opts: It was situated in a flat desert, making it easy to attack by cavalry.
It was naturally protected by rugged boulder-strewn hills and the river, providing immense defensive advantages.
It was completely open on all sides without any natural barriers.
It was located near the mouth of the Bay of Bengal, vulnerable to naval fleets.
practiceQuestions.sol: The capital city was strategically nestled in a basin surrounded by granite hill ranges and defended by the Tungabhadra River, making it exceptionally secure against surprise military assaults from northern sultanates. [Primary Reference: UNESCO World Heritage Site Report on Hampi / ASI]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the foundation of the Vijayanagar Empire:
1. The empire was founded by Harihara and Bukka in the year 1336 AD.
2. They belonged to the Sangama dynasty, which was the first of the four dynasties to rule Vijayanagar.
3. Sage Vidyaranya played a pivotal role in guiding the founders and establishing the empire.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All three statements are correct. Harihara and Bukka established Vijayanagar in 1336 AD under the Sangama dynasty, with the spiritual and political backing of sage Vidyaranya. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7 & 11 History]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about Deva Raya II of the Sangama dynasty:
1. He was the most prominent ruler of the Sangama dynasty.
2. He bore the title 'Gajabetegara' (hunter of elephants).
3. He refused to employ Muslim soldiers in his army due to religious orthodoxy.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Deva Raya II was the greatest Sangama ruler and took the title 'Gajabetegara'. Statement 3 is incorrect because Deva Raya II actively inducted Muslim archers and cavalrymen into his army to modernize it. [Primary Reference: Nilakanta Sastri, 'A History of South India']

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding foreign travelers who visited Vijayanagar during the Sangama period:
1. Nicolo de' Conti visited Vijayanagar during the reign of Deva Raya I.
2. Abdur Razzaq visited during the reign of Deva Raya II.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Nicolo de' Conti (Venetian) visited during Deva Raya I's reign around 1420 AD, and Abdur Razzaq (Persian ambassador) visited during Deva Raya II's reign in 1443 AD. [Primary Reference: NCERT Themes in Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the expansion and military campaigns of the Sangama rulers:
1. Kumara Kampana, son of Bukka I, successfully defeated the Madurai Sultanate and annexed Madurai.
2. Harihara II successfully extended Vijayanagar control over large parts of South India and captured important ports like Goa from the Bahmanis.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Kumara Kampana's conquest of Madurai is celebrated in 'Madura Vijayam', and Harihara II consolidated the empire, seizing key ports like Goa in the western coast. [Primary Reference: Standard Medieval History Sources / IGNOU]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding literary contributions under the Sangama dynasty:
1. Sayana wrote monumental commentaries on the Vedas with royal patronage.
2. Gangadevi, wife of Kumara Kampana, authored 'Madura Vijayam'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Sayana and his brother Madhava Vidyaranya produced crucial Vedic commentaries, and Gangadevi wrote 'Madura Vijayam' detailing her husband's southern expedition. [Primary Reference: NCERT Cultural History]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the decline of the Sangama dynasty:
1. Internal rebellions, weak successors, and military defeats against the Bahmani Sultanate and Gajapatis of Odisha weakened the dynasty.
2. Virupaksha Raya II was the last ruler of the Sangama dynasty, after which Saluva Narasimha took power in 1485.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The later Sangama rulers faced severe external pressure from the Bahmanis and Gajapatis alongside internal decay, leading to the usurpation of power by Saluva Narasimha in 1485 AD. [Primary Reference: IGNOU History / Standard Historical Textbooks]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding administrative and revenue divisions during the Sangama period:
1. The empire was divided into provinces known as Mandalas.
2. Mandalas were further subdivided into Nadus, Sthalas, and Gramas.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are accurate. The hierarchical administrative structure of Vijayanagar flowed from Mandalas (provinces) down to Nadus (district/county), Sthalas (groups of villages), and Gramas (villages). [Primary Reference: Epigraphical Evidence / NCERT]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the economic conditions under the Sangama dynasty:
1. Agriculture was the mainstay of the economy, with land revenue generally fixed at one-sixth of the gross produce.
2. Overseas trade was insignificant as the rulers prohibited merchants from sailing to foreign countries.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: land revenue was typically one-sixth of the produce. Statement 2 is incorrect because overseas maritime trade flourished extensively with Arabia, Persia, Southeast Asia, and China through ports on both the western and eastern coasts. [Primary Reference: Economic History of South India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the conflict zones between Vijayanagar (Sangama rulers) and the Bahmani Sultanate:
1. The Raichur Doab, situated between the Krishna and Tungabhadra rivers, was a primary bone of contention due to its extreme fertility and wealth.
2. Control over the Konkan ports for horse imports was another major economic and strategic reason for war.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The fertile Raichur Doab and lucrative western ports controlling horse imports were the two primary geopolitical drivers of perpetual warfare between Vijayanagar and the Bahmani Sultanate. [Primary Reference: NCERT History / Hermann Kulke]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding religious patronage under the Sangama dynasty:
1. While being devout Hindus who patronized Saivite and Vaishnavite institutions, the Sangama kings practiced religious tolerance.
2. Muslims were employed in the military administration, particularly as archers and cavalrymen during the time of Deva Raya II.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The Sangama rulers patronized Brahmanical institutions and sages while maintaining an inclusive administration that welcomed foreign traders and employed Muslim military specialists. [Primary Reference: Epigraphical Records & Standard Historical Texts]
